scope.summary: This run renders the real MCP App bundle in a real MCP Apps host, against a fixture MCP server. It qualifies the App side and the protocol libraries; it does not test the product server.
real: the MCP App bundle (ui/dist-apps/app.html), built by this run with the product build script
the View code in that bundle: the product Source, Changes, Timeline and Present views, with the chart and data table
the host implementation: the ext-apps basic-host example, in Chromium
fixture: the MCP server is okf-qualify-mcp-apps, this harness; it is not the product server
the render tools, show and read_object answer from committed files under tests/fixtures/views
read_object is declared with the product schemas from api/mcp-tools.json, but its handler is the harness
not_covered: the product server's show and read_object handlers
the product blob store and the product's authorization of a read
any host other than basic-host: claude.ai and ChatGPT belong to the gate mcp-apps-web-hosts
scope.reading_note: "dataset_exercised" and present_dataset.status "exercised" mean the App fetched the fixture dataset through the harness read_object and drew it. They do not mean the product read_object tool was called.

rules.bundle/single_app_resource: The bundle manifest this run built lists exactly one resource, ui://okf-jawn/app.html.
rules.bundle/mime_type: Every mimeType in that manifest is the ext-apps SDK's RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE.
rules.bundle/react_production_build: The built App bundle does not contain react-dom's development build: its DevTools notice is absent from the file.
rules.bundle/served_as_html: The harness, loading the bundle the manifest names, reads every resource back through its own resources/read handler as an HTML document.
rules.protocol/render_tools: tools/list lists exactly the four render tools, each with _meta.ui.resourceUri naming the shared App resource.
rules.protocol/app_only_tools: The tools whose _meta.ui.visibility is exactly ["app"] are read_object and show, and every listed tool is a render tool or one of these.
rules.protocol/read_object_declaration: The listed read_object carries the product's inputSchema and outputSchema from api/mcp-tools.json unchanged.
rules.protocol/resource_listed: resources/list lists exactly one resource, the shared App resource.
rules.protocol/resource_mime_type: resources/read returns text whose mimeType is the ext-apps SDK's RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE.
rules.protocol/resource_meta_ui: resources/read attaches _meta.ui.csp as an object with connectDomains and resourceDomains arrays.
rules.protocol/resource_is_built_bundle: The text resources/read returns hashes to the sha256 the bundle manifest of this run records.
rules.protocol/render_tool_results: Every render tool returns structuredContent for the App and a non-empty text block for hosts without Apps.
rules.protocol/show_bound_sources: show, called as PresentView calls it, returns the bound item and revision for every resolved binding of the present result.
rules.protocol/read_object_ranged_loop: read_object, called in PresentView's loop, serves each retained dataset in more than one block, each block naming the object and the offset asked for, until has_more is false.
rules.protocol/read_object_digest: The bytes assembled from those blocks hash to the binding's materialized digest, and total_size is their count.
rules.protocol/read_object_unknown_digest_refu: read_object answers a digest nobody retains with isError and no structuredContent.
rules.protocol/read_object_unknown_argument_re: read_object answers a request with an argument the product request type does not have with isError and no structuredContent, as the product's deny_unknown_fields does.
rules.render_source/text: In the App frame of the reference host, render_source shows the source view's own text for the committed fixture and none of another view's, and no waiting, disconnected or unparsed-result message.
rules.render_source/no_alert: The App frame holds no element with role="alert". Only the App frame is read: an alert in the host page or in the sandbox proxy frame is not seen by this rule.
rules.render_source/accessibility: axe analysed the App frame and found no serious or critical violation in it.
rules.render_changes/text: In the App frame of the reference host, render_changes shows the changes view's own text for the committed fixture and none of another view's, and no waiting, disconnected or unparsed-result message.
rules.render_changes/no_alert: The App frame holds no element with role="alert". Only the App frame is read: an alert in the host page or in the sandbox proxy frame is not seen by this rule.
rules.render_changes/accessibility: axe analysed the App frame and found no serious or critical violation in it.
rules.render_timeline/text: In the App frame of the reference host, render_timeline shows the timeline view's own text for the committed fixture and none of another view's, and no waiting, disconnected or unparsed-result message.
rules.render_timeline/no_alert: The App frame holds no element with role="alert". Only the App frame is read: an alert in the host page or in the sandbox proxy frame is not seen by this rule.
rules.render_timeline/accessibility: axe analysed the App frame and found no serious or critical violation in it.
rules.render_present/text: In the App frame of the reference host, render_present shows the present view's own text for the committed fixture and none of another view's, and no waiting, disconnected or unparsed-result message.
rules.render_present/no_alert: The App frame holds no element with role="alert". Only the App frame is read: an alert in the host page or in the sandbox proxy frame is not seen by this rule.
rules.render_present/accessibility: axe analysed the App frame and found no serious or critical violation in it.
rules.render_present/chart_marks: The chart svg holds exactly as many mark elements (children of g.role-mark) as the dataset has rows. Equality is right for this fixture because its chart is one unit bar with a plain nominal field against a plain quantitative field: Vega-Lite compiles that to one rect per row, and nothing aggregates, bins, stacks, filters or layers. The expectation is derived from the fixture; another specification is refused, not guessed.
rules.render_present/table_rows: A visible table captioned with the binding shows the dataset: the same columns, the same cells row by row in order, and every value in the visible text.
rules.render_present/chart_source_table: The chart's own "Source data" table (inside <details>) holds the dataset cell by cell: the same columns and the same rows in order.
rules.render_present/show_calls: While the view rendered, the harness server logged at least one successful show call.
rules.render_present/read_object_calls: While the view rendered, the harness server logged successful read_object calls for the dataset's digest that form one or more complete reads: each starts at offset 0, every block starts where the one before ended, and the last ends at the dataset's size with has_more false, after more than one block.
rules.render_present/no_refused_call: While the view rendered, the harness server refused no tool call.
rules.render_present/dataset_exercised: The App fetched the retained dataset through the harness read_object and drew it: every dataset rule of this view passed and the App frame showed no alert. Fixture evidence; the product server is not involved.
